messages:
anya: Heads up — after the v3.18 release I'm seeing ~35% p99 token latency increase on INT8 profiles for our chat models. Repro at low QPS. Dequant hotloop looks suspicious.
ci-bot: Perf alert: job/runtime-int8-regression — p99 +34% vs baseline. details: http://ci.internal/runs/789 (compare 3.17 -> 3.18)
mike: Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro? which model/seq/batch?
anya: gpt-like-2k config, seq=1024, batch=1, kv cache hit rate high. Repro script: infra/bench/quant_kv.sh (I pushed the run logs to /tmp/quant_regress.log)
li: Ran local bench with `--profile=hot`. Flamegraph shows most time in `dequant::apply` and repeated `kernel_selector::choose_kernel`.
sam: Starting git bisect now. If it's selector or batcher change it's likely the culprit.
sam: `git bisect start --bad v3.18 --good v3.17`
sam: `git bisect run ./scripts/bench_regress.sh`
sam: Bisect result: commit 4f7b2c9 — "refactor: prioritize float kernels for short seqs". The patch changes kernel priority table and selection heuristics.
anya: That commit forces float kernels for seq < 512, but our INT8 routing still falls back to dequant path because kernel compatibility check fails and we dequant/requant on each layer.
mike: Can we force quant kernel choice as a workaround? config flag?
li: Quick workaround: `runtime.config.force_quant_kernels = true` — that pins selection to quant kernels for INT* profiles. Doing that on a canary now.
mike: Rolling canary with flag on dedicated-pool-2 (2 nodes).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: service=runtime, env=dedicated-pool-2, canary=2/3
anya: Early canary numbers look back to baseline for p99. KV-cache invalidation rate drops too.
mike: Propose revert of 4f7b2c9 + follow-up that adds explicit kernel compatibility matrix so quant routing doesn't trigger dequant churn.
li: Also noticed KV cache miss rate spiked when kernel switched per-shard — kernel change invalidates cached KV blob keys (they encode kernel id). That's causing extra recompute and new cache entries.
anya: Opened PR #4279: revert 4f7b2c9 + unit test for kernel compatibility and a perf test `tests/perf/quant_kernel_routing.py` to run in CI. Added note to changelog.
ci-bot: Perf CI queued for PR #4279 — job: perf-guard/quant-routing (will run against baseline and PR)
sam: Notes from profiling: dequant/requant overhead is proportional to number of layer switches. For short sequences the per-switch overhead dominates; for long sequences it's amortized. Patch inadvertently increased number of switches for our quant path.
li: Long-term plan: add kernel compatibility matrix + routing that maintains KV cache key stability across kernel selection changes, and improve batcher heuristics to avoid oscillation.
mike: OK — merging revert once perf CI green. Thanks everyone for quick bisect and canary. :tada:
anya: I'll keep monitoring cluster metrics and post final p99 numbers here after merge. Thanks all.
